en: Read the Valley First: River, Hills, and East-West
zh: 先读河谷：黄河、两山与东西方向
ja: まず河谷を読む：黄河、二つの山、東西の方向

p.src: From the White Pagoda Hill side, Lanzhou's shape appears before its sights do. The Yellow River runs east through the valley; the city extends along both banks, held to a long corridor by nearby ridges. The Yellow River Iron Bridge is not the end of a route called “city centre.” It is one place to cross. On the first day, establish the bank you are on and whether the next stop lies east or west, then decide whether to cross. That habit is more useful than memorising a list of attractions.

caption.zh: 从白塔山一侧俯瞰，黄河铁桥只占河谷的一处横断面；真正决定路线的是下一站在东还是西、在南岸还是北岸。
caption.ja: 白塔山側から見下ろすと、黄河鉄橋は長い河谷の一つの横断地点にすぎない。経路を決めるのは、次が東西どちらか、南北どちらの岸かである。
caption.en: From the White Pagoda Hill side, the Yellow River Iron Bridge occupies one crossing in a long valley. The next stop's east-west position and riverbank determine the route.

p.src: The map keeps seven first-use anchors. Lanzhou West and Gansu Provincial Museum lie in the west. Xiguan and the Zhongshan Bridge-White Pagoda approach mark the central crossing. Dongfanghong Square, Lanzhou University, and Lanzhou Railway Station mark the east. The red and green links show the relationship of Metro Lines 1 and 2; they are not surveyed track alignments. The airport inset uses a separate scale. Use the map for the broad decision, then check entrances, transfers, and live operation before setting out.

caption.zh: 蓝线沿黄河向东；红、绿线只表示地铁连接关系。山地色带与机场框都是方向示意，不代替导航或当日运行信息。
caption.ja: 青線は黄河を東へたどり、赤線と緑線は地下鉄の接続だけを示す。山地の帯と空港枠は方向の模式図で、経路案内や当日の運行情報ではない。
caption.en: The blue line follows the Yellow River east; red and green show metro connections only. Hill bands and the airport inset are orientation devices, not navigation or live service information.

p.src: An official Gansu geography account describes Lanzhou's main urban area as extending more than forty kilometres east to west and narrowing to about one kilometre north to south. Those figures describe the city's form, not a visitor strip that can be walked end to end. When Lanzhou West and Lanzhou Railway Station fit on the same page, the distance between them is easy to underestimate. Both carry the city's name; they are not the same arrival point.

p.src: First: is the next stop east or west? Second: is it on the Yellow River's south or north bank? Third: if the bank changes, at which bridge or station will that happen? Fourth: is today's arrival or departure point Zhongchuan Airport, Lanzhou West, or Lanzhou Railway Station? Answer all four before choosing between the metro, a ride-hailing car, and walking. If one answer is unclear, return to the map before trusting a journey-time estimate.

p.src: For a first plan, divide the commonly used places into three working segments. In the west, use Lanzhou West and Gansu Provincial Museum. In the centre, use Xiguan, the Yellow River Iron Bridge, and the White Pagoda approach. Farther east, Dongfanghong Square, Lanzhou University, and Lanzhou Railway Station define an eastern station corridor. The segments overlap and are not administrative boundaries. Use them to keep luggage, the first visit, and dinner within one workable part of the city.

p.src: The central riverfront is easier when arranged as one line rather than a chase between sights. Complete the south-bank city section, then cross the Yellow River Iron Bridge, also called Zhongshan Bridge, to the north bank. Continue into White Pagoda Hill Park and read both banks on the same walk instead of making the park a separate out-and-back. If the lodging and dinner remain on the south bank, keep the return bridge and time in the plan. Other crossings or river services may be available, but do not count an unchecked option as a shortcut.

p.src: Straight-line distance omits station interiors, actual entrances, bridge approaches, changes in riverbank level, crossings, luggage, and the cost of choosing the wrong bank. Use the map for direction, then recalculate with a walking route that is usable that day. Add margin with a suitcase, for the White Pagoda climb, or before a reservation. A leg that works only when every exit is found immediately does not belong in a tight itinerary.

p.src: When Zhongchuan Airport T3 opened on 20 March 2025, passenger flights moved there from T1 and T2; check the terminal supplied by the airline again before departure. Rail requires the same precision. Lanzhou West and Lanzhou Railway Station are separate arrival gates, so the first leg begins at the station printed on the ticket. Confirm the full terminal or station name before connecting it to the lodging address and first stop. The next chapter handles the airport, West Station, and Lanzhou Railway Station separately.
